ASTRA STAGE ONE: WORKING MACHINERY TO A NEW ASSEMBLY QUESTION
1 November 2026

RECOMMENDATION

Select temporary, sequence-specific control of RNA-protein assembly for the
sustained second stage. The concrete target is an assembly constraint that
prevents premature docking, permits useful local folding, and then releases,
leaving a full-translation-active ribosomal subunit with fewer required assembly
services. Prefer naturally transient guides when they suffice; timed antidote
is an additional control whose material and process cost must earn its place.

This is an opening selected for further construction, not a completed device,
a demonstrated closed protein factory, or a historical novelty claim. The
central molecular selectivity and postbinding release are not established by
the kinetic model. What makes the opening timely is a concrete combination of
existing experimental traps, real structural data, a related RNA-bound release
operation, and strong new defined-assembly comparators.

WHY THE ELECTRICAL CONTENDER DID NOT WIN

The first root construction learned a local mechanical action Gram matrix from
thermal boundary-response fluctuations. It was checked in an exact lossless
Helmholtz scattering model against direct momentum flux. The key covariance
identity and the associated finite-observation theory remain useful.

The independent alternatives changed the decision. Active terminal-only probes
already learn task-specific improvement directions without internal coordinates.
A four-read positive-control experiment on one unreset trajectory cancels affine
drift; in a detector-limited example it beats a favorable passive covariance
oracle, while paying in displacement and work. A callback-only active controller
also reached a feasible complete electrical-response target in an inclusion
model. Electrical training of physically rearranging nanotube matter is already
demonstrated in a 2016 primary experiment.

Moreover, exact PSD control-cone and circular-planar response obstructions show
that knowing the response does not create arbitrary material capabilities.
No total observer/control/resource advantage was earned for this branch.

REMOVABLE CONSTRAINTS FOR ASSEMBLING RNA MACHINES
Stage-one construction, 1 November 2026

STATUS

This is a proposed physical construction, an ordinary kinetic analysis, and
executable finite-resource mechanism tests. No new ribosome has been made.
No molecular release rate, assembly yield, or historical priority is claimed.
The purpose is to decide whether a specific missing physical operation merits
the sustained second stage. The abstract kinetic model is not evidence that
a particular oligonucleotide realizes the assumed rates.

1. CAPABILITY AND THE DISCOVERY THAT CHANGED THE QUESTION

The consequential capability is manufacture of complex, functional RNA-protein
machines from sequence-defined inputs and a fully enumerated set of services.
A renewable protein factory is the demanding application: active output must
replace its translation and assembly machinery while leaving useful production
capacity. An extract that supplies an unknown assembly proteome is an input to
be replaced, not a solved part of the factory.

The starting operations were found independently of this destination:

* Sheng et al. (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-61640-1, physically capture
  ribosome assembly intermediates with antisense oligonucleotides. Their data
  include both inhibiting probes and a facilitative DNA-RA15 result. The actual
  iSAT system supplies S150 extract, native-derived ribosomal proteins, RNA
  modification activities and assembly factors. Their antidote rescue is
  PREHYBRIDIZATION of probe and antidote, not release of an already bound probe.
* Smart et al. (2024), DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae143, use a DNA splint with exposed
  tails on purified ligated 16S rRNA, then remove the bound splint using a fully
  complementary competing DNA at 46 C under conditions intended to preserve
  RNA higher-order structure. This earns a related postbinding release operation
  on RNA, not its transfer to a protein-coated assembly intermediate.
* Huang and Karbstein (2021), DOI 10.1073/pnas.2101164118, identify a natural
  mechanism in yeast small-subunit assembly: block a junction's tertiary
  interaction partner while the junction can refold, rather than necessarily
  binding the misfolding junction itself. It motivates a geometric gate target;
  it does not establish a bacterial synthetic gate.

source_excerpts.text:
SOURCE-TO-CONSTRUCTION DECISION: TEMPORARY RNP ASSEMBLY GATES
2026-11-01. Parent investigator owns the finite kinetic construction.

WHAT IS AVAILABLE

Sheng et al. 2025, Nature Communications 16:6642,
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61640-1
provides real ASO interventions in S150-based iSAT. DNA-RA15 facilitates the GFP
readout and targets a domain II junction. PNA-RA20 disrupts H1 and produces an
observed misdocked III/VI arrangement, including RA20-B-c. Biotinylated probes
co-localize with intermediate fractions. The reported antidote rescue neutralizes
the probe BEFORE the assembly reaction; it does not remove a prebound gate.
S150 supplies modification, processing, assembly and translation functions.
This is direct access to relevant physical states, but its helper inventory is
not defined. Exact conditions and missing sequence inputs are in
ASO_GATE_INPUTS.json. Sequences have not been invented or reverse-engineered
from helix names.

Smart et al. 2024, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae143,
https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/52/10/5950/7624078
provides a distinct real operation: a DNA splint is displaced from ligated 16S
rRNA using complementary DNA and terminal unpaired tails, at 46 C. The authors
preserve higher-order RNA structure. It supports removal from folded naked RNA;
it does not establish access, branch migration or post-release recovery in a
protein-coated, ASO-stalled 50S assembly intermediate. The source operation was
read independently by the parent investigator and is recorded with that scope.

Huang and Karbstein 2021, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2101164118,
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8237570/
supplies the biological mechanism worth abstracting: factors and snoRNAs bind
the tertiary partner l31 rather than the j34-35-38 junction itself, withholding
a docking interaction that would trap an incorrect local fold. Release then
allows the folded junction to dock. This is a rationale for selective partner
withholding, not a demonstration of a synthetic large-subunit guide.

PRIOR CONSTRUCTIONS THAT REMOVE BROAD NOVELTY CLAIMS

Lei et al. 2020, DOI 10.1016/j.giant.2020.100008,
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666542520300084
already constructs catalytic nucleic-acid chaperones for RNA/ssDNA hairpin
refolding, with large acceleration. Pokhrel et al. 2024,
DOI 10.1021/jacs.3c14350, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11135164/
